The only support is lab-only: 'reducing the minimum track length from 6 to 4 improved both embryo folds'. On their BH-0004 base (ref 56591286), a length of 6 removed 3,349 short-track nodes. (3) VALUE: this knob is a closed line in disguise. It is I-129 (LB probe 6 exp21: 4 -> 0.943, -0.002; 8 -> 0.944). Round 13 measured 7/9 on the x138 bed at -0.0003. FINAL_REPORT_v4 l.156 lists MIN_TRACK_LEN 4 among the births/optional-node levers that 'stay closed on the LB anchors', and every node-count LB lever was <= 0 (IDEAS l.226). A 2-fold in-sample lab gain with no LB read follows the edge-filter pattern (+0.016 lab, 0 LB). I-509 says the -0.002 anchor is old-base noise, but no positive evidence exists either, so E[gain] is about 0 or negative. (4) FEASIBILITY: 3 of 5 slots were used on 29 Sep (00:05, 00:05, 00:46Z). The 2 left belong to MORNING TABLE v1.1, and the 23:30Z FREEZE (CONTEXT l.3789) bars new arms. A build plus dummy (GPU about 3 h) could be submitted around 11-12Z. With a non-CI L of 7-8 h it would read around 19-20Z, which is at or after the 20:00Z tick and past R31-A3's 'a read after ~19:30Z cannot be a final'. So nothing reaches R8, and the finding stands with its evidence corrected.
